text: As the town hall clock struck the twelfth chime, Erubami paused.
He looked at his sleeping wife, his healthy children, and the peaceful warmth of his home.
He pulled his hand back, knelt beside the table, and whispered a prayer of thanksgiving.
The calabash glowed with a deep, approving amber light.
When morning arrived, the vessel remained as generous as ever.
Erubami returned to his handcart on Russell Street with a singing heart, knowing that the greatest magic on earth is not the gold that fills a purse, but the gratitude that satisfies the soul.
